stories.title: Rohail Nazir's fifty books Asia Cup Rising Stars semi-finals spot for Pakistan Shaheens
summary: An unbeaten half-century by Rohail Nazir, followed by a devastating bowling display, helped Pakistan Shaheens defeat Nepal by 96 runs in their final Group ‘B’ match of the Asia Cup Rising Stars at the University of Doha for Science and Technology on Tuesday.
Batting first, Pakistan Shaheens were in trouble at 66-6 in 16.5 overs before wicket-keeper-batter Rohail steadied the innings with an unbeaten 64 off 83 balls, hitting four fours and three sixes.
Hasnain and Sufyan took three wickets each for 21 and 17 runs respectively, while Imran claimed two for 29.

stories.title: Fazl decries ‘state siege’, claims prevented from attending Lahore event
summary: LAHORE: Police began removing barriers around Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s place of stay in Lahore on Tuesday evening, with the Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief claiming he had been put under an hours-long “state siege” to restrict his movement.

In an earlier video message, the JUI-F chief alleged that he was under a “state siege” and that roadblocks and checkpoints across Lahore were preventing him from attending a multi-party seminar organised by the LHCBA.

In a statement, the party’s spokesperson warned that arrests of JUI-F workers in different cities on Monday, followed by the alleged deployment of a heavy police contingent outside the party chief’s residence, would have political consequences for the government.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz assures KP governor of continued support to eliminate terrorism
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday assured KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi of all possible cooperation on behalf of the federal government for the complete eradication of terrorism, durable peace and the welfare of the public in the province.
The federal government would continue to “fully support the implementation of the decisions taken at the apex committee meeting to completely eliminate terrorism”, he was quoted as saying.

He reaffirmed the federal government’s commitment to providing full support for the development of KP and the welfare of its people, saying that all possible resources would be mobilised to provide them with healthcare, education and other basic facilities, according to the PMO.

stories.title: Govt selects consortium of 3 foreign banks for $500m finance facility backed by MIGA
summary: According to the ministry, the decision was taken in a virtual meeting held by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb with the senior leadership of a consortium of international banks and representatives of the agency.

The banks were selected on the basis of the most competitive financing terms offered to the government, it said. “The one-year facility, renewable on a rolling 1+1+1 basis, will support the financing of essential imports and trade-related expenditures,” the statement said.

The ministry said the government would work closely with MIGA and the selected banks to advance the transaction towards its timely execution, looking forward to building strong and lasting relationships.

stories.title: Media monitor launches campaign to 'raise better sons' in effort to combat gender-based violence
summary: They were paid less than men,” Dr Tauseef pointed out, while talking about enlightened countries and societies which saw women at par with men and how quickly they developed.
The Uks director also pointed out that one thing ingrained in boys from childhood was that they were not supposed to cry. “If crying is only for women, then how come men have tear glands?

Senior journalist and activist Sohail Sangi said that there had been different attitudes towards women through the ages. “Behaviours and attitudes have changed with religions and regions,” he said. “I hail from Tharparkar where we had not even heard of things such as ‘karo kari’.

stories.title: Islamabad United snap up Matt Henry, Karachi Kings secure Adil Rashid as direct signings for PSL 12
summary: Islamabad United have signed New Zealand fast bowler Matt Henry, while Karachi Kings have secured the services of England leg-spinner Adil Rashid as their marquee direct signings for the 12th edition of the Pakistan Super League (PSL).
Multan Sultans have also utilised the direct-signing facility, bringing Australian fast bowler Lance Morris on board ahead of the player auction scheduled for January 23, 2027.

The direct-signing window, which opened on October 23 and closed on November 23, allowed each of the eight franchises to recruit one overseas marquee player who did not feature in either PSL 10 or PSL 11.

stories.title: Reacting to Bilawal's remarks on 'brute majority', a section of legal community wants 26th, 27th Amendments repealed
summary: In an open letter on Tuesday, 100 individuals — mostly lawyers and also including activists and academics — called for both the 26th and 27th Amendments to be repealed. “Pakistan’s constitutional order belongs to its people.
The 26th Amendment carved a constitutional bench out of the SC, with its members chosen by a reconstituted Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) in which judges no longer held a majority.

However, a majority “made up with seats that were unjustly denied to the opposition is not the majority the Constitution demands”, they contended. “An amendment passed on that basis holds no constitutional, legal, or democratic validity.

stories.title: Punjab Assembly adopts resolution seeking tougher punishment for blasphemy
summary: LAHORE: The Punjab Assembly on Tuesday unanimously passed a resolution demanding legislation to make the punishment harsher under Section 298-A (use of derogatory remarks, etc, in respect of holy personages) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC).
The House urged the federal government to move on the matter on a “priority basis” and enact legislation needed to increase the penalty under Section 298-A.
In August 2023, Parliament passed the Criminal Law (Amendment) Bill 2023 to increase the punishment under Section 298-A from three years of imprisonment to at least 10 years in jail.

stories.title: 'Carrying hopes of 250m people': Zeeshan Ali to be 'first' Pakistani astronaut in space aboard China’s Shenzhou-24
summary: Zeeshan Ali was named a crew member of China’s Shenzhou-24 space mission on Tuesday, which is scheduled to launch on November 25, with Ali set to become the first Pakistani to undertake an orbital space mission.
And the Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said the Pakistani astronaut was also the first international crew member to join China’s manned space programme.
PM Shehbaz had hoped that the space mission would “add new dimensions to the brotherly relationship between Pakistan and China”.

stories.title: Hours-long road closures around Karachi’s PIDC junction cause traffic congestion
summary: KARACHI: Commuters in Karachi’s Saddar area faced traffic congestion on Tuesday after authorities closed some roads around the PIDC junction for a few hours in response to a sit-in call by the Sindh Indus Lawyers Forum (SILF).
In an alert issued at 1:16pm, Karachi Traffic Police said both roads from PIDC Chowk towards the State Life Building, as well as Dr Ziauddin Ahmed Road, were closed to traffic.
In an update at around 6pm, the traffic police said the cut from PIDC Chowk towards State Life Building and both sides of Dr Ziauddin Ahmed Road have been reopened to commuters.

stories.title: COP collapse
summary: This omission was rejected by the EU, Britain, and some small, climate-vulnerable states, which rightly hold fossil fuels responsible for global warming.

Ironically, many of the countries that opposed the deal for not including the transition away from fossil fuels, refused to move forward on earlier pledges to provide and mobilise funding for poor climate-vulnerable countries.

It has been noted, in fact, that many of the latter prefer funds over curbs on fossil fuels at this stage, given their need to rehabilitate lives already impacted by climate change and build infrastructure strong enough to withstand future shocks.

stories.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill 7, including senior security official
summary: Israeli airstrikes in Gaza on Tuesday killed seven people, including Hamas’s director of internal security, Palestinian officials in the territory told AFP, despite a ceasefire in place since last year.
Police station strike Bassal said earlier on Tuesday that three people, including a 17-year-old, had been killed in a separate Israeli airstrike near Gaza City.
Israel’s military said it “struck terrorists in the area” of the police station, but did not confirm the strike that killed the 17-year-old.

stories.title: 'Watching me with eyes of fire': Pope Francis revealed in personal diary having seen devil
summary: The late Pope Francis recounted seeing the devil three times and, on one occasion, the “gate of hell”, in excerpts from his personal diary published on Tuesday in a new book.
Francis wrote that he recalled three episodes “when I don’t doubt he was physically present”. “More or less fifteen years ago.
During the second episode inside a Carmelite chapel, Francis wrote: “He was watching me with eyes of fire”. “I can’t forget that gaze, stronger than the previous.

stories.title: Freedom of speech should not become a shield for those crossing 'red lines', says Naqvi
summary: He alleged that only 47 per cent of the complaints made by the Counter Terrorism Department were acted upon by social media platforms. “This is not about technology, this is about people.
The minister called for moving from policy towards enforcement. “To begin with [social media] platforms, OTT services and major content creators must register with the authority.

Naqvi then went on to recount a recent town hall meeting, where he met five girls who were on the verge of ending their lives due to someone about to release “sensitive material” on social media platforms. “We don’t have any pathway for approaching those platforms.

stories.title: Eight killed, seven injured as passenger vehicle plunges into ravine in KP's Torghar
summary: At least eight people, including two women, were killed and seven others injured on Tuesday when a passenger vehicle plunged into a deep ravine in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Torghar district, Rescue 1122 said.
Earlier this month, three people were killed and 13 others injured when a coach collided with a motorcycle in Dera Ismail Khan.
Earlier in the month, at least eight people were also killed and 30 others injured when a passenger bus collided with a truck near the Havelian Interchange on Hazara Motorway.

stories.title: The state of Pakistan's mental health
summary: https://www.dawn.com/news/2045903

stories.title: Balochistan announces rewards of up to Rs250m for information on most-wanted terrorists
summary: The Balochistan government has announced cash rewards ranging from Rs500,000 to Rs250 million for individuals providing credible information about the province's most-wanted terrorists.
The provincial government announced the rewards through an official advertisement, a copy of which was also shared on X by Babar Yousafzai, the chief minister's assistant on home affairs.
On November 13, security forces killed 74 terrorists during operations in Balochistan and Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa.

stories.title: FBR to set up sales tax zones in Karachi, Lahore, Islamabad, Multan
summary: The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) is establishing separate sales tax zones in Karachi, Lahore, Islamabad and Multan to improve sales tax collection, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif was informed on Tuesday.
The development was shared during a weekly review meeting on FBR affairs, chaired by the prime minister in Islamabad, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office.

Regarding the FBR’s digital operations, the meeting was informed that additional security features had been incorporated into several software systems operated by Pakistan Revenue Automation Ltd (PRAL) to ensure data integrity.

stories.title: Second supermoon of 2026 lights up skies across Pakistan
summary: Supermoon rises over Karachi, Pakistan https://t.co/C5Fsaa4qwe — Reuters (@Reuters) November 24, 2026 According to NASA, a supermoon occurs when a full moon coincides with the moon being at or near perigee — the closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit.
NASA said a full moon at its closest point to Earth could appear up to 14% larger and 30% brighter than the faintest full moon of the year, which occurs when it is farthest from the planet.
The third supermoon of the year is expected on December 24, according to NASA.

stories.title: Speakers call for social media accountability, balanced regulation to curb disinformation
summary: Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said Pakistan had nearly 100 million social media users and around 160 million smartphone users, making the spread of unverified information a major challenge.

He said the shift from traditional to social media had transformed the information landscape, allowing anyone with a smartphone to produce and disseminate content and making verification increasingly difficult.
Memon urged social media platforms to deploy artificial intelligence and other tools to identify harmful content, particularly material inciting violence.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz congratulates CDF Munir on Hall of Fame induction at Malaysia’s National Defence Studies Centre
summary: On Monday, ISPR said CDF Munir would also visit the National Defence Studies Centre, where a formal ceremony would be held to induct him as the 21st member of its “prestigious” Hall of Fame.
In a meeting with Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim on Monday, CDF Munir reaffirmed their shared commitment to strengthening bilateral defence ties in Putrajaya.
CDF Munir also held a meeting with Malaysian Defence Minister Mohamed Khaled bin Nordin.

stories.title: ‘The universe has no borders': Pakistan's historic space mission draws global praise
summary: Pakistan's first astronaut mission entered its final stages, with Muhammad Zeeshan Ali set to make history as the country's first astronaut to travel to China's Tiangong space station aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft.
Together, let's go further." Congratulations to Muhammad Zeeshan Ali from Pakistan for becoming the first foreign astronaut to board China's #Tiangong space station!

Pakistan is poised to send an astronaut into space for the first time on Wednesday, when air force pilot Muhammad Zeeshan Ali joins China’s Shenzhou-24 mission to the country’s Tiangong space station.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz takes notice of provocative statements by cabinet members, urges them to settle differences amicably
summary: ISLAMABAD: Amid rising political tensions, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday took notice of provocative statements by the federal cabinet members against each other and directed them to resolve their differences through consultation.

The remarks come amid a war of words between coalition partners over the past few days regarding a proposed referendum on the creation of new provinces, with a federal cabinet member publicly expressing his grievances against a colleague.
On Monday, PML-N Senator Rana Sanaullah said Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had “complicated” the matter of creating new provinces by making an “irrelevant speech at an irrelevant forum”.

stories.title: Russia’s Sputnik news agency launches Urdu service
summary: The launch comes amid growing engagement between Islamabad and Moscow in trade, energy and diplomatic affairs, with both countries seeking to broaden their bilateral partnership.

Describing its editorial focus, Sputnik Urdu said the service would offer Urdu-speaking audiences coverage of international affairs, global politics, breaking news and in-depth analysis, connecting them with developments from around the world.
The development comes ahead of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's official visit to Russia, as the two countries look to expand cooperation across multiple sectors.

stories.title: Cricket's saliva ban to stay despite Indian skipper Shubman Gill’s call to overturn rule
summary: The International Cricket Council has no plans to reverse the ban on applying saliva to shine the ball, despite India skipper Shubman Gill’s call to allow the practice again.
Gill on Monday said the ban should be revoked to help bowlers get reverse swing, after India’s high-scoring opening Test in Wellington against New Zealand ended in a draw.
The Indian Premier League lifted its saliva ban last year, much to the bowlers’ delight, but the ICC finds no reason to relax it in international matches.

stories.title: PTI moves IHC for live broadcast of Al-Qadir Trust case hearing
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) has filed a petition in the Islamabad High Court (IHC), seeking live broadcast of the appeal proceedings in the £190 million Al-Qadir Trust case involving party founder Imran Khan.

It argues that the case is a matter of national importance and that live broadcasting of Imran’s appeal proceedings is essential to ensure transparency, uphold justice and maintain public confidence in the judicial system.

The petition argues that live broadcasting would allow an independent assessment of all legal aspects of the case and requested the IHC to order the live broadcast of the complete proceedings of the appeal.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz assures K-P governor of federal support to eliminate terrorism
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday assured Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Governor Faisal Karim Kundi of the federal government's full support for eliminating terrorism, restoring lasting peace and ensuring the welfare of the people in the province.
During the meeting, Governor Kundi briefed the prime minister on efforts being undertaken by his office and the K-P Advisory Council to improve law and order in the province.
On November 8, Governor Kundi called for greater political ownership of the fight against terrorism, as the provincial government announced a new plan to strengthen the police and CTD.

stories.title: Imran wants PTI to expand political alliance, extend outreach to Fazl and other opposition parties, core committee told
summary: ISLAMABAD: The PTI’s core committee has been informed that incarcerated party founder Imran Khan wanted it to expand its “political alliance” and extend outreach to Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman and other opposition parties.

The PTI issued a statement after Khosa briefed the party’s core committee on the meeting. “The core committee was informed that Imran Khan had expressed his complete confidence in the opposition leadership.

Reiterating its previous demands, the committee “urged the honourable judges to take immediate and serious notice of the matters raised in Imran Khan’s letter and ensure the prompt implementation of judicial orders concerning his medical treatment”, the statement said.

stories.title: US blacklists Alibaba subsidiary and Megaspeed linked to Nvidia scandal
summary: The US Commerce ​Department on Monday added Megaspeed and Alibaba's Singapore subsidiary, which has business ties to the cloud company at the center of the Nvidia scandal, to its trade blacklist, ‌following criticism from lawmakers and administration officials.

Megaspeed, an Nvidia partner which has been under investigation by US authorities since 2024 over whether it diverted AI chips to China, will now need approval from the US Commerce Department to obtain US exports, which is likely to be denied.

Besides Megaspeed International and Apex, the Commerce Department on Monday added five other companies related to the cloud firm, including its owner, Swiftdata, and its Malaysian subsidiary Speedmatrix, to the Entity List.

stories.title: Naqvi says govt has no intention of curtailing freedom of expression, warns against crossing 'red lines'
summary: The Interior minister said the establishment of the Social Media Protection Regulatory Authority (SMPRA) would help the government address online crimes and ensure social media platforms respond promptly to complaints from victims.
Naqvi criticised social media platforms for acting on only 47% of the government's requests to curb terrorism-related content.

Social Media Platforms (SMPS) and the Post-truth Era https://t.co/0L6j1absLV — SDPI (@SDPIPakistan) November 24, 2026 Referring to cases of online harassment, the minister said five female victims of cybercrime had recently met him during an open court hearing.

stories.title: Tech firms soar as Huang’s return reinvigorates AI trade
summary: Technology firms rocketed Tuesday as Asia joined a global stock surge following the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia boss less than two weeks after stepping down over extramarital affairs including with an alleged Chinese spy.

News of his return — announced soon after the opening bell Monday — lit a fire under equities, sending shares in Nvidia soaring an eye-watering 31.5 per cent and adding more than $900 billion to the firm’s market value.
The United States on Monday added Megaspeed to a trade blacklist that bars it from purchasing advanced chips.

stories.title: Germany, Italy, Poland, Sweden join France to set up international AI defense center
summary: Germany, Italy, Poland and Sweden joined France to set up an international artificial intelligence center for defense, the French Defense Ministry announced on Monday.

"Germany, Italy, Poland and Sweden officially announced their intention to join the International Center for Artificial Intelligence in Defence (ICAID), during the center’s first establishment conference held in Rennes on November 19 and 20," the ministry said in a statement.
"The next step will be to work with the participating nations on drafting the center's founding texts with the goal of reaching full operational capability in the course of 2027."

stories.title: Collision between bus, truck kills 11 in UAE
summary: According to the ministry, emergency teams were dispatched to the accident site immediately after receiving the report.
The ministry urged the public to exercise caution, rely on official sources for information and refrain from circulating rumours or unverified reports about the accident.
It is the second major road accident to occur in the UAE this month.

stories.title: Pakistan down South Korea to keep final hopes alive
summary: Rana Waheed Ashraf was also on target for Pakistan while Chun Semin and Lee Minhyeok scored for South Korea in an encounter that went down to the final minute.
South Korea reduced the margin once again in the 60th minute when Lee converted a penalty corner, but Pakistan held on to secure three crucial points.
All three of Pakistan's goals came from field play, while South Korea scored one field goal and one from a penalty corner.

stories.title: Pope Francis had visions of the devil and hell, diaries reveal
summary: The late Pope Francis suffered a two-year spiritual crisis starting in 2021 when he felt tempted by the devil and struggled with how to wield power over the Catholic Church, a new collection of his private diaries published on Tuesday revealed.

Read: Pope Leo first pontiff to cast US ballot Cardinal Victor Fernandez, a close Francis collaborator, collected the diaries – the first by a pope to be released to the public since the 1960s – and arranged them into a volume with his own accompanying commentary.

An entry from January 2021, at the beginning of the late pope's self-described spiritual crisis, lists three times throughout Francis' life when he thought he had seen the devil, including once as pope in a meeting with Vatican officials.

stories.title: YouTube star Ms Rachel protests US child immigration hearings
summary: Ms Rachel, the American creator of hit sing-songy educational videos for toddlers, attacked the use of immigration hearings for children following a courthouse visit on Monday.

"I've seen children who are just missing the light in their eyes and they're begging to go to the spelling bee or to just, you know, be with their younger siblings," said Ms Rachel, who is known offline as Rachel Accurso.
"I think it's sad to take someone's dedication and love for all children and try and make that wrong," she told PBS last year.

stories.title: Life returning to Tirah with return of displaced persons
summary: KHYBER: With the return of nearly 2,000 selected displaced persons to the restive Tirah Valley since last week, a number of shops in the main market have reopened after 11 months of closure.

Sources among the returned persons told Dawn that shops mostly dealing in edibles, medicines and construction tools were reopened with the return of at least 60 shopkeepers of Lar Bagh Markaz in Maidan area, the main trading centre of Tirah Valley.

Suhbat Khan Afridi, a spokesman for the displaced Tirah residents, told this scribe that though shops at Lar Bagh Markaz had reopened on a limited scale, reconstruction or repair of the damaged houses was a difficult exercise for them.

stories.title: Investigation launched as ‘diphtheria’ claims life in KP's Bajaur
summary: BAJAUR: The health department on Monday launched measures against suspected diphtheria cases after the infection left a child dead and infected two others in War Mamund tehsil of Bajaur district.
When contacted, District Health Officer Dr Gohar Ayub confirmed to Dawn the death of a girl child and the infection of two others.

He said as per the investigation, the infection was initially reported in the area about two weeks ago, with a 10-year-old child, Hasham Khan, developing fever, sore throat and other symptoms on Nov 12.

stories.title: UK 'Grand Theft Auto VI' hacker gets 7-year sentence
summary: Having already served years in custody, Arion Kurtaj, aged 21, was entitled to walk free immediately, Judge Mark Turner said at London's Woolwich Crown Court.

Kurtaj, who is autistic, pleaded guilty last week to hacking major companies between 2021 and 2022, including GTA-maker Rockstar Games, mobile operator BT/EE, digital bank Revolut and ride-hailing giant Uber.
In the 2023 trial, another member of the Lapsus$ group, who was 17 at the time, was found guilty of hacking chip titan Nvidia in February 2022 and threatening to release its intellectual property.

stories.title: Sheikh Hasina seeks to return to Bangladesh on December 16 on state carrier
summary: Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return home from more than two years of exile in India on December 16, her spokesperson told Reuters on Tuesday, though the government said she can only return through extradition.

Hasina has denied the charges from exile. “She can only return home by extradition treaty; in handcuffs, and under strict surveillance,” Humaiun Kobir, Bangladesh’s minister of state for foreign affairs, told Reuters.

A Bangladeshi minister told Reuters on Sunday that Hasina would be arrested and jailed on return and that there had been no official discussions with India about sending an aircraft to bring her back.
